summary: The cast is right. The strokes show 5 donkeys and 2 drivers. Every donkey whose head can be read faces east-south-east, and the west driver holds a stick out over the last donkey, driving from behind. So the train walks east, down toward the bridge's east end, as t8 recorded (D1 is a side view like D2, not end-on). The tree count of 19 in the range agrees trunk by trunk, and t7's crossing reading of the three bare elms holds. The pale patch at 35907-35980 is ground strokes, not a man. The boat lies afloat on the pale water, between the spit, the bank's foot and the bridge. Its bow can't be read: no rudder or sweep. Proposed: one new entity, a vertical pole at the boat's east end. It is about 60 px long and stops 40-60 px short of the nearest bridge post, so it reads as a mooring pole, not the rope the notes describe. Also proposed: 15 changes. Three only correct notes (the train's direction, the boat, the bridge). Eight are the extents the merge asked about. The near bank, and with it the stream's south shore, runs on east to about 37250, not 36850. spit_36225 reaches a tip at (36815, 1433), 165 px past its mapped tip. The shoal starts at about 35790. The pale band's north shore at 35500-35780 is at v about 1390, not 1330. In 34850-35850 neither the pale band nor the near bank has any edge on the silk. The seals start further east than the notes say: 37396 for the strip at v 805-1007, 37362 for v 1138-1351. So the north bank's foot line runs visibly between them to the silk's end at about 37560. The east spit runs to the seal at 37362 and reappears past it at 37568-37610. The bank at the east trees' feet has its foot at the lowest stroke of its layered wash, v 918-978, about where the road's edge_n is. The mapped 868-870 is an upper layer. Smaller items: D1's head measured, the west driver's confidence raised, and the slender tree's foot moved 18 px west to its trunk's centre.

lessons: **Measure a seal before you stop a line at it.** S1's east end stopped the road and three bank lines at u 37250 'under a seal'. The seals there sit at u 37396-37538 (v 805-1007) and 37362-37567 (v 1138-1351); the one at 37248 is at the top of the silk (v 51-319). So 150 px of painted bank and the strip between the seals were left out. Find each seal's box from its red pixels (R-G > 45 on the scan), run every line to the box it really meets, and say in the note where the strokes show again past the seal.

**A layered wash bank has its foot at its lowest stroke.** Countryside banks are painted as two or three stacked wash strokes with paler gaps between them. The lower edge of the first stroke is a layer, not the bank's foot (S1.grd.bank_37050: mapped 868-870, drawn foot 918-978). Take the foot from a column darkness profile through the whole band, and check it against the figures and the road beside it: the drivers stand and the road runs along the true foot.

**A line at a boat's end: follow it to both ends before naming it.** A rope runs to what it is tied to and slants toward it. A vertical line that rises from the boat and stops short of everything is a pole planted in the bed (S1: 60 px long, ending 40-60 px under the nearest bridge post). Check the post the note names against the structure's own `bays`.

**Read a pack animal's view from its legs, not from its load.** Two bundles side by side can be a front-and-back load seen in profile. Legs spread along u mean a side view (S1's D1: three legs 37 px apart, head lowered at the east end). An end-on animal shows its panniers left and right of a central head or rump, and its legs splay to both sides (D5).
